content.value_statement: Multiplayer games require deliberate choices about authority, synchronization, latency, bandwidth, and abuse prevention. This skill provides concise principles for planning those systems.
actual_capabilities: Compares dedicated, peer-to-peer, host-based, client-server, and distributed multiplayer architectures.
Explains state synchronization, input synchronization, and hybrid synchronization approaches.
Outlines prediction, interpolation, reconciliation, and lag compensation techniques.
Suggests bandwidth controls including delta compression, quantization, priorities, and areas of interest.
Applies server-authoritative validation principles to movement, combat, inventory, and hidden information.
Identifies matchmaking factors such as skill, latency, wait time, and party size.
limitations: Provides principles and planning guidance, not production-ready networking code.
Does not select a game engine, transport protocol, hosting provider, or networking library.
Does not calculate infrastructure capacity, operating cost, or regional deployment requirements.
Requires environment-specific testing for latency, packet loss, scale, security, and gameplay behavior.

use_cases.title: Choose a Multiplayer Architecture
use_cases.description: Compare server models against game pace, player trust, operating cost, and expected scale.

use_cases.title: Plan Network Synchronization
use_cases.description: Define update rates, synchronized data, prediction, interpolation, and reconciliation for responsive play.

use_cases.title: Review Multiplayer Security
use_cases.description: Evaluate server authority and validation rules for movement, combat, inventory, and hidden information.

prompt_templates.title: Select an Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend a multiplayer architecture for [game type], [player count], and [latency target]. Compare security, cost, complexity, and host migration needs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when starting a multiplayer game design.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Synchronization Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a synchronization plan for [gameplay systems]. Specify state or input sync, update rates, prediction, interpolation, reconciliation, and server authority.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when defining how clients and servers exchange gameplay data.

prompt_templates.title: Reduce Network Bandwidth
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this multiplayer data model: [details]. Propose delta compression, quantization, priorities, areas of interest, and event-based updates with tradeoffs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when bandwidth or scale is a concern.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Competitive Game Integrity
prompt_templates.prompt: Threat-model this multiplayer design: [details]. Identify client trust assumptions, validation gaps, hidden-data exposure, duplication risks, and latency abuse. Prioritize mitigations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for an advanced security and anti-cheat review.

output_examples.input: Choose an architecture for a four-player cooperative action game with moderate latency sensitivity and limited hosting budget.
output: Recommended model: host-based play with clear host authority and migration planning.
Synchronize player inputs and important state while validating combat and inventory changes.
Test host latency, disconnect recovery, cheating exposure, and migration behavior before release.

output_examples.input: Plan synchronization for a competitive arena game with movement, health, projectiles, inventory, and chat.
output: Send movement at a controlled rate with prediction, interpolation, and reconciliation.
Update health and inventory on change, while sending chat only when submitted.
Keep combat validation and inventory ownership on the authoritative server.

output_examples.input: Review a design where clients report successful hits and receive every enemy position.
output: High priority: validate projectile paths, timing, player state, and sight lines on the server.
Limit hidden enemy data with relevance filtering to reduce wall-hack exposure.
Measure how validation and filtering affect latency before deployment.

best_practices: Make the server authoritative for competitive state and validate every client claim.
Design for realistic latency using prediction, interpolation, reconciliation, and lag compensation.
Send only necessary data at rates matched to each gameplay system.
anti_patterns: Do not trust client-reported movement, hits, inventory changes, or timing without validation.
Do not send all world data when relevance filtering can protect bandwidth and hidden information.
Do not require exact remote positions when interpolation and prediction provide smoother results.

faq.question: Which multiplayer architecture does this skill recommend?
faq.answer: The recommendation depends on game pace, scale, budget, latency, and security needs. The skill compares several common models.

faq.question: Does this skill generate networking code?
faq.answer: No. It provides architecture and design guidance that must be implemented with your selected engine, protocol, and networking library.

faq.question: What synchronization methods are covered?
faq.answer: It covers state synchronization, input synchronization, hybrid approaches, prediction, interpolation, reconciliation, and lag compensation.

faq.question: How does the skill address cheating?
faq.answer: It recommends server authority, movement and combat validation, server-owned inventory, and restricting hidden data.

faq.question: Can it help reduce bandwidth usage?
faq.answer: Yes. It discusses delta compression, quantization, priorities, areas of interest, event-based updates, and appropriate update rates.

faq.question: Does it replace multiplayer testing?
faq.answer: No. You must test latency, packet loss, disconnects, scale, security controls, synchronization, and gameplay behavior in the target environment.
